back.text: ctx.enqueue_function[kernel](...)
back.markdown:
## `ctx.enqueue_function[kernel](...)`

```
ctx.enqueue_function[vector_addition](
    lhs_tensor,
    rhs_tensor,
    result_tensor,
    grid_dim=num_blocks,
    block_dim=block_size,
)
```

The kernel is a compile-time parameter; the data and dimensions are arguments.

back.markdown:
## From the built-in index structures

```
from std.gpu import block_idx, thread_idx, block_dim

var tid = block_idx.x * block_dim.x + thread_idx.x
```

`global_idx` computes the same flattened index for you.

```
from std.gpu import block_idx, thread_idx, block_dim
```

{#0F766E}The split is deliberate: low-level primitives that describe the execution model stayed in `std`, while host and runtime APIs live in `max`.{/}

back.text: ctx.synchronize()
back.markdown:
## `ctx.synchronize()`

```
ctx.enqueue_function[kernel](..., grid_dim=g, block_dim=b)
ctx.synchronize()
```

{#C62828}Reading a result before synchronizing reads whatever was there.{/} {#0F766E}It is a barrier between the host and the device, and it costs real time — enqueue everything you can before you call it.{/}

front.text: How is shared memory allocated in a kernel?
front.markdown: How is shared memory allocated in a kernel?

back.text: stack_allocation with the shared address space
back.markdown:
## `stack_allocation` with the shared address space

```
from layout import stack_allocation

stack_allocation[dtype, address_space=.SHARED](layout)
```

Shared memory is on-chip and visible to every thread in the block — the staging area for a tile.

back.text: The last dimension is contiguous
back.markdown:
## The last dimension is contiguous

```
row_major(rows, cols)
```

Adjacent columns of one row sit next to each other in memory. {#0F766E}Column-major is the transpose of that convention — adjacent rows of one column are contiguous.{/}

front.markdown: Why does row-major versus column-major matter so much on a GPU?

## `barrier()`

```
from max.gpu.sync import barrier
```

Every thread in the block waits until all of them have arrived — the call you need between filling shared memory and reading it.

front.markdown: What is the rule about where a `barrier()` may appear?

```
from max.gpu.sync import syncwarp
```

It takes an optional `mask`, defaulting to all threads — for coordinating threads that have diverged inside one warp.

```
if global_idx.x < Int(size):
    ...
```

{#C62828}The grid is sized in whole blocks, so the last block almost always has threads with nothing to do.{/} Without the guard they read past the end.

front.text: How do you debug a Mojo GPU kernel?
front.markdown: How do you debug a Mojo GPU kernel?

back.text: mojo debug --cuda-gdb --break-on-launch
back.markdown:
## `mojo debug --cuda-gdb --break-on-launch`

```
mojo debug --cuda-gdb --break-on-launch \
  --vscode myproject.mojo
```

`--break-on-launch` stops as the kernel launches so you can set breakpoints in device code. {#C62828}NVIDIA GPUs only.{/}

front.text: Why use breakpoints rather than stepping in a GPU kernel?
front.markdown: Why use breakpoints rather than stepping in a GPU kernel?

back.text: Stepping does not work reliably on the GPU
